sentences.text: Documents are taken on record.

This is the first criminal appeal filed by the appellant under Section 14-A ( 2 ) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act for grant of bail relating to FIR No.
18 of 2024 registered at Police Station Sabalgarh, District Morena (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376 (D), 294, 506 of the I.P.C. and Section 3(2) (5), 3(1) (w)(i) of SC and ST Act.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant argued that the appellant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in this case.
Allegedly, the incident occurred on 12/01/2024.
However, the prosecutrix has not lodged any report or filed any complaint at the concerned police station despite the fact that she is a major woman.

It is further submitted that present FIR is an outcome of monetary dispute which is evident from CCTV footage filed along with the bail application, in which, the prosecutrix and the appellant / accused can be seen in a Bank doing transaction.
It is further submitted that the prosecutrix also called from her mobile phone and details of the call is annexed along with the application.
There is material improvisation in the facts narrated in the FIR and the statements given in the police station as well as concerned Magistrate by the prosecutrix.

In the FIR allegation of rape has not been made against the present appellant, however, in her statement recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C she improvised her version and made allegation of rape against the appellant.
The case of the prosecution is medically belied.
There is no reason why the prosecutrix did not inform her husband for four days about the incident.
Learned counsel for the appellant further argued that the appellant is in custody since 16.01.2024.
He is the permanent resident of District Morena (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Hence, he prays for grant of bail to the appellant.
O n the other hand, learned State counsel as well as counsel for the complainant opposed the appeal and prayed for its dismissal.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting upon the merits of the case, this appeal stands allowed and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- (Rs. One Lakh only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court.
